proposal.observation: Round-1 overlay (denoising z_step 0.0015 / grad 0.20; enhancing curvature 0.006 / inter_radius 0.06; detecting binary 140, oblique 44, horizontal 84, maxLineGap 60) was valid but rejected: proxy 0.6140 -> 0.6035, correspondence_f1@15 0.282 -> 0.262 (-0.020), depth_nan_ratio 0.120 -> 0.114 (better), sam_fill_rate and ring_count_error unchanged. The before/after detected_lines.png are nearly identical: the same red/green oblique segments on the right half, the same blue horizontal fallback segments, only one extra short red segment near (1100, 2300) and slightly longer blue segments. initial_prompt_points.png before/after are pixel-identical: three 'assume' centres at x=120/360/600 (y~1120/1555/1120), the lone negative-slope centre at x=850 (y~1640), and the x=1810 midpoint still at y~2290 while the other right-half centres alternate ~1210/~1640. So the moderate Hough relaxation did not change a single prompt centre - consistent with the ontology note that on 1-1 the vertical-line fallback makes moderate stage-4 Hough changes unidentifiable - and the F1 loss must come from the joint denoising/enhancing change altering depth-map edges without moving prompts. The left four rings (x<1000) still show only sparse dotted joint pixels in the outlier map, and raising binary_threshold to 140 in round 1 could only have thinned them further.
proposal.rule: d7 still fires (m_line_yield low on the left half AND horizontal fallback engaged) -> f_missing_lines; upstream suspect f_joint_oversmoothed (faint joints from the low-density far-from-scanner half). Round-1 feedback adds a constraint: small deltas inside the detecting stage are below the identifiability floor on this scan, and the denoising/enhancing perturbation of round 1 was net negative for F1. Therefore push r_relax_hough to the bound edge in one direction only (lowest oblique threshold, largest maxLineGap, lowest binary threshold so faint joint pixels survive binarisation), strengthen joint enhancement only via inter_radius, and leave denoising at the incumbent.
proposal.failure_mode: stage_4_detection.f_missing_lines (left-half rings receive 'assume' centres; prompt phase drifts by ~90 px between halves and by ~one block height at x=1810), upstream stage_3_upsample.f_joint_oversmoothed; the round-1 denoising/enhancing perturbation is retracted as a non-helpful joint change.
proposal.rationale: Stage 1 is locked, so unfolding is untouched. Denoising keys are omitted so they return to the incumbent (round 1 showed the combined denoising+enhancing move cost F1 while changing nothing in stage 4). Detecting: binary_threshold=100 (bound minimum) keeps the faint left-half joint pixels that round 1's 140 suppressed; hough_threshold_oblique=40 (minimum) and maxLineGap_oblique=80 (maximum) give the oblique HoughLinesP its best chance to bridge the dotted joint lines at x<1000 into accepted oblique segments so those rings stop receiving 'assume' centres; hough_threshold_horizontal=90 (maximum) keeps the lower binary threshold from adding horizontal fallback lines from border/speckle rows. Enhancing: inter_radius=0.08 (maximum) increases the interpolation radius of enhance_outlier_points so joint points on the sparse half are densified; curvature_threshold is left at incumbent. This is a deliberate bound-edge probe in the direction all three worked examples agree on (the two better outcomes s005/s002 used low oblique thresholds 44/47; the catastrophic s011 used 76), with sam y_bounds, hough_threshold_vertical and mask_r untouched because ring count, depth_nan_ratio and sam_fill_rate remain healthy. If prompt centres still do not move, the next round should conclude that stage-4 knobs are saturated on this scan and turn to the remaining upstream/SAM knobs. Outcome is a joint effect of the full overlay; no per-parameter causal claim.
